employmentPathway:
MountMove's strong partner and client networks in Nigeria and internationally provide a foundation for connecting programme participants with employers. We will use these relationships to identify business needs, secure industry contributions and develop progression opportunities linked to participants’ demonstrated capabilities.

Our employment pathway will begin at onboarding. Each participant will complete a skills assessment and career discussion, producing an individual progression plan. We will identify suitable occupational pathways, such as junior data analysis, digital operations, technical support and business support, matching these to programme content and realistic employer requirements.

Before and during delivery, our Business Growth and Advisory Lead will engage clients, partner businesses and industry contacts to identify relevant vacancies, skills gaps and project opportunities. We will seek specific commitments, including employer project briefs, mentoring time, workplace exposure and interview opportunities. Confirmed commitments will be recorded separately from prospective opportunities.

Participants will then undertake practical projects that reflect workplace expectations. Where businesses can contribute suitable briefs, learners will address genuine operational challenges using appropriately anonymised information. Trainers and industry mentors will assess technical work alongside communication, reliability, teamwork and problem-solving. Each participant will build a portfolio showing their contribution, methods and results.

The Training and Incubation Lead will coordinate employment preparation alongside technical learning. Support will include CV development, professional profiles, applications, interview practice and presenting project work. Host career services, where agreed, will help connect participants with existing employer engagement activities and relevant recruitment channels.

Towards programme completion, we will organise employer showcases and targeted introductions. Participants who demonstrate readiness will be referred for suitable vacancies, paid internships, entry-level positions or paid project assignments. International contacts will also be approached for appropriate remote opportunities, subject to employer requirements and participants’ readiness.

For participants requiring additional support, particularly NEET youth and women facing participation barriers, mentors will provide individual guidance and application follow-up. We will discuss accessibility needs and practical constraints early, helping participants assess opportunities against their circumstances and sustain engagement through recruitment.

We will maintain an employer opportunity register and track each participant’s movement from portfolio completion to referral, interview, offer and accepted opportunity. Follow-up at 30, 90 and 180 days after programme completion will record progression and continuing employment, using participant reports and employer confirmation where consent permits.

Employment, paid internships, freelance assignments and business creation will be reported separately. Confirmed job placements will require evidence of employment starting. Our aim is to convert industry relationships into documented recruitment opportunities and sustained progression, giving employers evidence of capability and participants structured support towards meaningful work.

The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) reports to the Board and provides overall executive leadership. Chief Operating Officer (COO) responsible for programme implementation, operational coordination, stakeholder management and oversight of delivery teams. 
Chief Financial Officer (CFO) responsible for financial management, budgeting, expenditure controls, financial reporting and supporting compliance with financial and contractual obligations.

The organisation also incorporates legal, policy and compliance capacity into programme implementation. Recent documentation identifies experience in developing internal policies for regulatory compliance, corporate governance and the review of legal instruments relevant to public-private and development-sector engagements.

Board of Directors → Chief Executive Officer → COO / CFO → Programme & Technical Leads → Specialist Teams / Facilitators / Operational Staff
programmeDeliveryTrackRecord:
Codextel Limited has a strong track record in designing and delivering large-scale education technology, creative skills development, digital learning, and capacity-building programmes across Nigeria. Its programmes have served diverse cohorts including young people, students, teachers, creative professionals, facilitators, and in-school and out-of-school learners. Codextel's delivery model combines curriculum development, practical skills training, digital learning tools, creative content, facilitator development and community-based implementation. Its educational engagements have reached over one million learners through digital learning platforms and terrestrial media, while thousands of teachers, students and creative professionals have participated in its training and capacity-building initiatives. 

A significant example is in the N-Power Creative Programme, where Codextel Limited served as a lead implementing partner for creative digital skills training across the South-South and South-West regions of Nigeria. The programme targeted young people seeking employable and entrepreneurial skills within the creative economy. Codextel facilitated training in storytelling, animation, illustration and post-production, combining technical instruction with practical exposure and internship facilitation through creative hubs. This strengthened participants' practical competencies and supported pathways into employment, entrepreneurship and the wider creative industry.

Codextel also delivered programmes focused on STEAM education and digital skills development. Over a two-year engagement, the company designed and implemented creative skills hubs and deployed digital education tools and STEAM Labs across schools in Nigeria. Teachers and facilitators were trained to effectively manage these learning environments, while students gained access to hands-on learning in Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics. A further one-year programme involved administering STEAM Labs for both in-school and out-of-school learners, providing practical learning infrastructure designed to strengthen problem-solving, collaboration and readiness for future careers in technology and the creative industries.

In digital education, Codextel has developed interactive learning platforms aligned with the Nigerian National Curriculum, digitising subjects such as Mathematics, English, Basic Science, and Civic Education into accessible and engaging formats. Through our flagship education content, Codex Learn, the company has adopted visual, auditory and story-based approaches to learning while supporting teachers in integrating digital tools into classroom delivery. Codextel has also developed Hausa-language educational content to improve accessibility for learners in underserved communities and different cultural contexts.

Beyond education and training, Codextel has demonstrated capacity in public-sector communication and policy engagement. Under the Nigeria Economic Sustainability Plan (NESP), the company developed digital platforms and 2D/3D animated explainers to simplify national policies for public understanding. Codextel also provided communications support to the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC), including policy advisory services and market surveys supporting strategic communications and public-sector implementation frameworks.

Overall, Codextel's programme history demonstrates the ability to design curricula, mobilise and train cohorts, establish and operate learning environments, train facilitators, develop digital learning solutions and deliver programmes across multiple Nigerian regions. This combination of nationwide programme delivery, creative-industry expertise and education technology capability provides a strong foundation for Codextel's role as an Enterprise Support Organisation (ESO) within the iDICE ecosystem.

Data would be maintained in structured beneficiary records and programme databases, with appropriate disaggregation by gender, location, programme/skill track and beneficiary status, allowing progress against inclusion and programme targets to be monitored.

employmentPathway:
Codextel Limited employs a structured training-to-employment and entrepreneurship pathway designed to move beneficiaries beyond skills acquisition into practical industry experience, paid work, self-employment and entrepreneurial opportunities.

This approach has been demonstrated through the N-Power Creative Programme, where Codextel trained over 1,500 young Nigerians in storytelling, digital illustration, 2D/3D animation, voice acting and post-production. The programme combined technical training with entrepreneurial development and practical industry exposure.

Most importantly, Codextel established and managed partnerships with animation studios and other creative-sector organisations to provide beneficiaries with structured internship opportunities. The programme documentation describes these arrangements as creating direct pathways to employment and entrepreneurial ventures within Nigeria's creative industry.

Codextel's employment pathway can therefore be represented as:
Beneficiary Recruitment → Skills/Aptitude Assessment → Technical & Creative Training → Practical Projects → Entrepreneurship & Employability Development → Portfolio Development → Industry Exposure → Structured Internship/Placement → Employment, Freelancing or Enterprise Creation.

Under the iDICE programme, this model will be strengthened through the following mechanisms:
Industry-Relevant Training: Beneficiaries will receive practical training aligned with current opportunities in the digital and creative sectors, supported by project-based learning and portfolio development.

Portfolio and Work-Readiness Development: Participants will complete practical projects that demonstrate their capabilities to prospective employers and clients. Employability preparation will include professional profiles, portfolios, CV development, interview readiness and workplace orientation.

Industry Mentorship and Exposure: Creative and technology professionals will be engaged as mentors, facilitators and industry advisers, enabling beneficiaries to understand workplace expectations, commercial standards and available career pathways.

Internships and Industry Placements: Codextel will leverage relationships with creative studios, digital businesses, partner organisations and other employers to facilitate internships, apprenticeships and work-placement opportunities. This builds directly on Codextel's previous N-Power Creative internship model.

Freelancing and Entrepreneurship: Because employment in the creative and digital economy extends beyond conventional salaried jobs, beneficiaries will also be prepared for freelancing, contract work and enterprise creation, supported through entrepreneurship development and incubation.

Post-Programme Tracking: Beneficiary progression will be monitored beyond training to track internships, employment, freelance engagements, enterprise creation and other economic outcomes.
